_note: ILLUSTRATIVE placeholder answers for the RC-1 Grid-to-Chip demo bid (OPP-0003), unit EP2 (Electrical Power Products, EP²): written for the PoC from the unit's point of view, not real unit positions. No certification, rating or date in them is verified. The design engineer answers the technical items, the unit manager the others.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP² supplies the MV control power as a 110 VDC battery and charger system fitted in its control enclosures, sized for the switchgear close and trip loads. The dual underground MV feeds on diverse, concrete-encased paths are civil and utility works outside EP²'s scope.
answers.reason: L1.08 (110 VDC control power with battery backup) is offered in full; L1.07 (dual concurrently maintainable MV feeds below ground with concrete encasement) is civil and cabling work that EP² does not deliver.
answers.conditions: Battery autonomy and charger sizing to be confirmed against the Owner's load schedule at design review.
answers.next_steps: The bid desk to assign the MV feeder duct banks to the campus civil contractor or the Owner's design consultant.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: The relay and protection panels use communicating protective relays with event and fault recording, and one relay per lineup can act as the remote terminal unit where the Owner asks for it. The communication protocol and point list are fixed with the Owner at design review.
answers.conditions: Owner to state where an RTU function is needed and its protocol.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP²'s protection engineers will support the Owner's interconnection studies and supply relay settings and protection-coordination data in the format the serving utility asks for.
answers.conditions: Depends on the utility's source data and its review timetable.
answers.next_steps: Agree the data exchange format with the utility at kickoff.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP² will install and connect any Owner-furnished equipment that interfaces with its protection panels and control enclosures, so that it works as part of the overall data center design.
answers.conditions: Owner to supply data sheets and wiring details of the furnished equipment before design freeze.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP² includes operator and maintenance training on its relay panels, control enclosures and DC power systems, delivered on site before handover.
answers.next_steps: Training plan and dates to be set in the project plan.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP² will use the PUE figures and energy price the Owner publishes during the dialogue to state the energy losses and running cost of its auxiliary power equipment for the total cost of ownership.

Illustrative placeholder response: EP² offers five years of maintenance and support from acceptance with a 24 by 7 support line and a four-hour remote response for its protection and control equipment. On-site attendance within four hours cannot be promised from the unit's current service base.
answers.reason: EP² has no field service team near the site, so a guaranteed four-hour on-site response, and the 6-hour and 2-hour repair times, cannot be committed for its panels.
answers.conditions: Repair times for compute cabinets do not apply to EP² equipment.
answers.workaround: Four-hour remote diagnosis by phone and remote access, an on-site spares kit (spare relays and charger modules) that the Owner's trained technicians can swap, and an EP² engineer on site within the next business day.
answers.next_steps: The bid desk to check whether a Flex field service team in the region can cover on-site response for EP² equipment.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP² can deliver its panels and control enclosures in phases that follow the deployment units, with the first phase shipped alongside the core infrastructure.
answers.conditions: Phase quantities to be fixed in the delivery and installation plan.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Each EP² panel and enclosure goes through a factory acceptance test, and EP² supports site testing, commissioning and the 30-day availability test for its equipment.

Illustrative placeholder response: EP² will submit its quality assurance and factory test plan at least 30 days before the factory test, covering wiring checks, relay injection tests and simulated faults such as loss of DC supply. Burn-in and benchmarks apply to the compute systems, not to EP² equipment.

Illustrative placeholder response: EP² will take part in the 60-day acceptance period, including the resilience test, where its protection and DC control power systems can be faulted in a controlled way to show the system stays safe.
answers.conditions: Fault-injection steps on protection equipment to be agreed in the acceptance test plan.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP²'s delivery follows the three phases of integration, validation and operational readiness, with its equipment commissioned and documented before operational readiness is declared.
Illustrative placeholder response: EP²'s project manager and lead design engineer will attend the kickoff meeting within 45 days of award.

Illustrative placeholder response: EP² will feed its risks, such as component lead times and design-freeze dates, into the risk management plan and register within 30 days of award and update them monthly.
Illustrative placeholder response: EP² will provide its engineering, manufacturing and delivery milestones for the project plan within 90 days of award and update them each quarter.
Illustrative placeholder response: EP² will fix its panel configurations, one-line diagrams and relay schedules at the technical decision point 9 to 12 months before delivery.
answers.conditions: Changes after the decision point may extend lead times and are handled as change orders.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP² will supply its input to each plan on time: footprints, weights, heat loads and cable entries for site preparation, its test steps for the acceptance test plan, shipping and installation details for each delivery, and the relay and SCADA communication links for the network plan.
answers.conditions: The bid desk consolidates the plans; EP² supplies its part only.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP² will give the safety data and handling, storage and disposal instructions for its station batteries as its input to the chemical management plan, nine months before delivery.
Illustrative placeholder response: We give guaranteed delivery dates for the panels of each deployment unit with the tender, stated as weeks from award.
answers.reason: DL-10 asks for guaranteed delivery dates; before award only dates counted from award can be guaranteed. They become calendar dates at contract signature.
answers.conditions: Delivery periods hold if drawings are approved within the agreed review time.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP²'s prices are firm, all-inclusive and in US dollars, free of taxes, and cover delivery to site, installation support, commissioning and training. They are split into equipment, freight, installation, commissioning, spares and five years of maintenance, with any later extension priced as an option.
Illustrative placeholder response: EP²'s prices are unconditional and contain no 'to be discussed' items or references to separate contracts.
Illustrative placeholder response: EP²'s offer stays valid for four months after the submission deadline.

Illustrative placeholder response: If the bid is successful, the performance guarantee, any pre-financing guarantee and the performance and payment bonds would be issued at Flex group level and cover EP²'s share of the contract.
answers.conditions: Form and issuing bank to be approved by Flex treasury before signature.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We accept liquidated damages for missed service levels, capped by the at-risk amounts described, and delay penalties that scale with the length of the delay and the seriousness of the breach, subject to an aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together.
answers.reason: Liquidated damages and delay penalties have no overall limit as written, which leaves an open-ended risk on a phased multi-lot delivery.
answers.workaround: An aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together, set as a percentage of each lot's price; the percentage is stated in the financial offer and listed in the commercial exceptions schedule (CT-08).

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our commercial exceptions are listed in the separate exceptions schedule and kept to a minimum: on liquidated damages, only the aggregate cap per lot asked for under CT-07; any indexed price is shown there only as an alternative to the firm price.

Illustrative placeholder response: Warranty on EP² equipment is included in the five-year maintenance period, with component warranties running inside it. EP² takes responsibility for failures caused by disturbances that stay within the Section 9 interface limits.
answers.conditions: Disturbances outside the Section 9 limits are excluded.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We provide a supply-chain security and risk plan for our panels, with approved alternative sources for sensitive components such as protective relays. Instead of a guarantee for each original component over the system's whole lifetime, we commit to the availability period stated as the proposed change.
answers.reason: No supplier can guarantee every original component for an open-ended system lifetime: electronic parts follow their makers' life cycles.
answers.workaround: Spare parts or compatible form-fit-function replacements available for at least 10 years from acceptance, with at least 12 months' notice of end of life and a last-time-buy offer before any component is discontinued.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP² accepts that it bears its own bidding costs and that the Owner may abandon the procurement before signature without compensation.

Illustrative placeholder response: Support for EP² equipment would come from its Des Moines base together with the Flex group's regional field service. Whether a Flex centre in the site's region meets every criterion (more than two years in the region, two similar clients, six English-speaking staff) still has to be confirmed.
answers.reason: EP² runs no support centre of its own in the site's region; the qualifying centre and its references depend on the Flex group's presence near the site, which is not yet stated.
answers.next_steps: Confirm the qualifying regional centre with the Flex group service organisation.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP² can name an experienced project manager and a protection and control specialist for the data center infrastructure role, each with more than three years in that role.
answers.reason: The systems architect, systems engineer and application and benchmarking specialist roles fall outside EP²'s products and must come from the compute and integration units.
answers.conditions: Names and CVs to be confirmed before submission.
answers.next_steps: The bid desk to complete the expert list with the other units.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP²'s place in the bidding group will not change between submission and award, and it can support the group leader with a reference from a comparable protection and control project.
answers.conditions: The reference customer's consent is needed before it is named.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP² will give its capital cost (equipment, site preparation needs and five-year maintenance) and its operating cost (energy losses of its auxiliary power and maintenance after year five) in the Owner's cost-performance format.
Illustrative placeholder response: EP²'s guaranteed delivery periods go into the bid's delivery schedule so the Owner can evaluate them and plan around them.
answers.conditions: Periods count from approved drawings, as stated for DL-10.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: EP² notes that the Owner will compare each lump-sum price with its engineer's estimate. EP²'s price breakdown is set out so that the comparison is easy to make.
Illustrative placeholder response: EP² will take part in the qualification, the dialogue sessions and the site visit, and will contribute to the final tender if the bid is invited.
